strengths: Clear problem formulation distinguishing between two sources of CLIP's BoWness (missing information vs. misalignment), providing valuable diagnostic insight
Comprehensive experimental validation through multiple complementary approaches (linear probing, robustness tests, conjunctive search) across diverse datasets (synthetic and real-world)
Convincing evidence that binding information exists in uni-modal embeddings: high linear probe accuracies (0.96 CLEVR image, 1.00 text) and robustness to multiple objects
Practical LABCLIP method with minimal overhead (262K vs 151M parameters), enabling post-hoc deployment without retraining encoders
Excellent presentation, clear writing, and thorough supplementary material supporting reproducibility
Thoughtful dataset design (PUG:SPARE) removing positional biases and improving evaluation rigor
weaknesses: Limited novelty: core finding (binding exists uni-modally but misaligned) is somewhat intuitive; linear transformation recovering binding follows logically from linear separability observation
Method does not advance SOTA: LABCLIP matches but does not exceed NegCLIP, contradicting claims of significant improvement; real-world gains are modest (ARO: 0.63→0.69)
Narrow scope restricted to attribute-object binding only; other compositional phenomena (spatial reasoning, negation, counting) explicitly excluded; only evaluates CLIP

Methodological concerns: linear probing measures linear separability but may not capture distributed binding encodings; synthetic BoW baseline is artificial; no statistical significance testing, error bars, or confidence intervals

Inconsistencies unexplained: LABCLIP hurts single-object classification (Table 11) without adequate justification; modality gap increases on CLEVR contradicting other datasets; LABCLIP-CC3M underperforms LABCLIP-COCO suggesting limited generalization

Real-world evaluation gaps: improvements much smaller on real datasets than synthetic (Tables 3 vs 4); modest ARO improvements; no failure case analysis; spatial reasoning shows limited transfer without explicit supervision

Missing analyses: why linear transformation is effective when CLIP's contrastive loss should encourage alignment; what structures matrix A learns; deeper investigation of binding representation in embedding space
Reproducibility issues: code availability URL missing in abstract; dataset generation requires specialized tools (Blender, Unreal); comparison with Lewis et al. (2024) relegated to appendix
